extracted_content: To enable encrypted inference using Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) schemes like CKKS, the Foundation Model (FM) must be redesigned because FHE only supports polynomial operations (addition and multiplication). The BlindFed framework replaces standard non-linear transformer operations with low-degree polynomial approximations: Softmax is approximated using a Taylor series expansion for the exponential function; GELU is replaced by a quadratic function (0.125x² + 0.25x + 0.5); and the division steps in LayerNorm and Softmax are implemented via Goldschmidt’s algorithm. Furthermore, the architecture is modified to use parallel adapters (LoSA) instead of sequential ones (LoRA) because sequential adapters would require backpropagation through the FM, which is computationally infeasible when data remains encrypted. This redesign allows the server to perform encrypted forward passes while the client trains the adapter on plaintext intermediate representations.

key_figures.caption: FHE-friendly architecture redesign. Each transformer block’s non-linear operations – GELU activations, Softmax attention, and the division step in LayerNorm – are replaced with low-degree polynomial approximations (denoted “Quad” for GELU and “ASoftmax” for Softmax). A lightweight parallel adapter and classification head are then trained on the client side.
key_figures.relevance: This figure provides the visual blueprint for the architectural changes described in this scene, showing exactly which components are replaced.

key_tables.caption: Softmax approximation results. Latency is computed per a batch of samples, when batch size is set to 8. One-epoch accuracy refers to the accuracy we obtain when performing one full pass over the data for only one epoch. This experiment is carried on the Fed-ISIC2019(center=0) dataset.
key_tables.relevance: Demonstrates the trade-off between the degree of the polynomial approximation (d) and the resulting model accuracy and latency.

key_tables.caption: Approximation of the reciprocal (inverse function). Latency is computed per a batch of samples (aggregate over L transformer blocks), when batch size is set to 8. One-epoch accuracy refers to the accuracy we obtain when performing one full pass over the data for only one epoch. This experiment is carried on the Fed-ISIC2019 (center=0) dataset.
key_tables.relevance: Shows the effectiveness of using Goldschmidt’s algorithm to approximate the division operation required for LayerNorm in an FHE context.

key_equations.relevance: Defines the Taylor series approximation used to replace the exponential function in Softmax.
The specific quadratic polynomial used to replace the GELU activation function.
